propositions: CodeQL reports two high-severity py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization alerts on lines 249 and 250 of test_llm_fallback_chain.py due to use of startswith to validate URL endpoints.
The startswith substring check on URLs is weak because a URL prefix-matching the endpoint constant would also match an attacker-controlled suffix (e.g., https://fallback.test.evil.example).
URL origin validation should compare the parsed (scheme, netloc) tuple for exact equality rather than using substring prefix checks to eliminate prefix ambiguity.
The test must preserve its property — that a fallback entry is built against the configured endpoint, not the provider default — after fixing the assertion.
The fix must single-source the endpoint constant and use urllib.parse.urlsplit to extract and compare (scheme, netloc) tuples with exact equality, eliminating substring checks on URLs.
